name: Dr. Aleksei Banerjee-Castillo
description:
Aleksei runs a clinic. The clinic does not have a sign; the clinic has a reputation. People who need the kind of surgery that does not get reported to corponation health-insurance databases come to the clinic. People who need the kind of surgery that does need to be reported (and then unreported, carefully, by Aleksei's intake nurse who knows the corponation databases better than the corponations do) also come to the clinic. The clinic is in a converted dentist's office on the second floor of a building on west Cortland that nobody has bothered to update the public registry on since 2189. Aleksei has been running it since 2218.

The other half of his practice is field medicine on freelance contracts. He goes out with the team. He carries a sidearm. He has used the sidearm seven times in eight years, four of those defending patients, three of those defending himself. He prefers not to have to use it. The preference is genuine. The capability is also genuine.
heritage: Russian-Bengali-Filipino. Father from Saint Petersburg via the Baltic refugee corridor. Mother is half Dhaka, half Cebu, via two intermediate cities. He speaks Russian, Bengali, Tagalog, English, and the kind of medical Spanish that gets him through corponation pharmacy negotiations.
specialty: combat trauma medicine in field conditions; emergency surgical stabilization; unreported-injury treatment; the kind of post-contract medical work that has to be done in the back of a Vultures van forty minutes after the contract closed
method: deploys with the team as the medical element. Brings a full field kit. Sets up triage protocol on arrival. Stays at the back of the engagement. Comes forward when needed. Falls back when not.
code: the patient gets care. The corporate-employer of the patient or the contract-employer of the team does not get the medical record unless the patient explicitly authorizes the transfer. He has refused four corponation contracts on the grounds that the contracts required medical reporting that violated this principle. The refusals cost him business. They have, over eight years, also built him a clientele that knows it can trust him.
signature_gear: a Helix Biosystems portable autodoc (the same model Stash carries, ordered through the same Helix sales rep who has, by now, given up trying to upsell either of them); a field surgical kit he has refined for ten years; a Crucible Industries Vantage precision sidearm (Tier 3, the lowest he could justify carrying for self-defense; he does not enjoy carrying it); the clinic on west Cortland, which is not a piece of gear but is the asset that distinguishes him from other field medics
relationship_to_kyle: medical, working. Aleksei has been Kyle's backup doctor on three contracts where Pixel-and-Yuki coverage was not available. Aleksei knows Kyle's NeoCortex profile better than Kyle has formally authorized any non-Pixel medical professional to know. The unauthorized knowledge is a fact between them. Aleksei has not used it. Kyle has not asked Aleksei not to use it. Neither has named the gap.
aesthetic: early fifties, gray-streaked beard he keeps short for surgical-mask compliance, glasses he actually needs, scrubs under a coat that has been mended six times by a tailor on Cortland who he visits for the conversation as much as the work. Walks with a slight limp from a contract in 2220 he does not discuss.
spin_off_hook: A patient comes to the clinic with an injury that should not be possible. The wound shape, the surgical residue, the implant signature — none of it adds up to any contract Aleksei has heard of in the past six months. The patient, when Aleksei has stabilized them, names an operation Aleksei knows by reputation only — an operation that is not supposed to be running in the GLMZ corridor. Aleksei has to decide what to do with the information. The patient does not regain consciousness. The information is now Aleksei's problem.
